stem.en: Contour trenches and bunds are made along a hillside at one height, not straight down the slope. Why?

text.en: So that water runs down the hill more quickly.

feedback.en: Faster water carries more soil. These measures do the opposite.

text.en: So that they lie across the water and slow it.

feedback.en: Right. Water meets them, slows down and soaks in.

text.en: So that the rain falls on a smaller part of the hill.

feedback.en: The same rain falls on the hill. What changes is how the water moves.

text.en: So that the rocks under the hill stop weathering.

feedback.en: They are built to slow water and hold soil, not to stop weathering.

explanation.en: Water runs straight down a slope. A trench or bund along a contour line lies across that path, so the water slows, soaks into the ground and leaves its soil on the hillside.

hints.en: Which way does water run on a slope? Which way does the trench run?
